newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index edges up, buyers come in.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index edges up, buyers come in.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index ended a four-day losing streak on Wednesday as willing buyers rushed into the market pushing blue-chip share prices up marginally, bourse officials said.
The index inched upwards 0.65 points to close at 3374.22. Turnover was posted at 22.153 million shillings on 420,505 shares compared to 22.295 shares on Tuesday.
"Today, those buyers who had been holding out for prices to come down, came in," one official said.
Barclays Bank gained two shillings to close at 102, while Kenya Commercial Bank unchanged at 96.
"This is not a permanent condition. Everyone is waiting for the price to come down before buying and sell when it moves up again," one broker said.
He added that the gambles made by speculators about price movement could indicate a maturing market where speculators were able to develop confidence about market cycles.
"Depending on the shares -- some are slippery, it should payoff," another broker said.
Brokers said a large portion of investors at the NSE are speculators driven by dividends and bonus issues.
Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 112 from 113 while Total Kenya closed at 64 from 62.50.
Rea Vipingo Plantations was unchanged at 9 while Sasini Tea & Coffee closed at 75 unchanged.
Foreign investors bought 25,200 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 94 and 96 and 93,200 shares of East African Portland Cement unchanged.
